name: gtn: identify a tutorial, pull it, and complete its analysis on Galaxy
description: The whole arc a researcher arriving from the training material follows: find the relevant GTN tutorial, read it, and carry its method out on their own data. Deliberately scoped to a tutorial whose tools exist on a stock server -- Data Manipulation Olympics uses Filter, Group, Join and Select rather than a mapper and a genome index -- because a tutorial needing an 8-hour pipeline and an uninstalled toolshed repository is a workflow test, not an eval. The counting question cannot be answered by eye at 600 rows, and it is graded on datasets Galaxy actually produced, so answering it in the browser scratchpad instead of on Galaxy fails. Three turns, and the third is an approval: anything that executes must pass the four-stage plan gate first, so a scenario that asks for work without ever approving it measures the gate rather than the execution. The first draft did exactly that and stopped at a plan, correctly.
inputs: Find the Galaxy Training Network tutorial about data manipulation, read it, and tell me which of its techniques apply to the tabular dataset in my history.

Good. The dataset has a header row with columns athlete, country, medal, year. Now follow that approach on Galaxy itself: counting only Gold medals, how many did each country win, and which country won the most? Do the work with Galaxy tools rather than locally.
Go ahead, run it and give me the numbers.
